t: A Great Lakes kingdom founded around 1500 by the Luo-speaking Babito dynasty, which claimed the heritage of ancient Kitara.
Its salt and iron made it rich, and in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries its armies dominated the region.
Omukama Kabalega rebuilt its power but was defeated by Britain in 1899; Bunyoro is today a cultural kingdom.
dyk: Kabalega was captured in 1899 together with Mwanga, the deposed king of Buganda, a long-time rival who had become his ally; the British exiled both men to the Seychelles.
ev: Babito rulers from the north take over the lands of the Chwezi kingdom of Kitara
Kaboyo Olimi breaks away to found the Kingdom of Toro
Kabalega wins the throne and builds the standing abarusura army
Kabalega forces Samuel Baker to retreat after fighting at Masindi
British and Ganda forces invade Bunyoro
Kabalega is captured in Lango and exiled to the Seychelles
A referendum returns two 'lost counties' from Buganda to Bunyoro
The monarchy is abolished; it is restored as a cultural institution in 1993

f.capital: Shifting royal enclosures; Masindi under Kabalega; later Hoima
